citeAs: Mo Li, Songyang Zhang, Taolin Zhang, Haodong Duan, Yunxin Liu, Kai Chen (2025). NeedleBench: Evaluating LLM Retrieval and Reasoning Across Varying Information Densities. Transactions on Machine Learning Research.
creator: Mo Li, Songyang Zhang, Taolin Zhang, Haodong Duan, Yunxin Liu, Kai Chen (Tsinghua University, Shanghai AI Laboratory)
description: NeedleBench is a comprehensive synthetic benchmark framework designed to assess retrieval and reasoning performance of large language models in bilingual long-context tasks with adaptive context lengths (e.g., 4k, 8k, 32k, 128k, 200k, 1000k, and beyond). It includes information-sparse tasks (Single-Needle Retrieval, Multi-Needle Retrieval, Multi-Needle Reasoning) and an information-dense task (Ancestral Trace Challenge), systematically embedding key data points at varying depths to rigorously test models' capabilities in diverse settings.
name: NeedleBench
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Approximately 10% of observed errors from the ATC task were manually annotated, focusing on cases where the question type is "identifying the eldest ancestor." Error types identified include: Under-thinking (60.2%), Partial Understanding Error (12.9%), Instruction Following Error (7.5%), Repetitive Output (7.5%), Hallucination Error (7.5%), and Other Errors (4.5%). Additionally, outputs of two smaller models (Qwen1.5-1.8B-Chat and Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct) were manually checked for instruction-following errors related to the \boxed{} format requirement.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset is synthetically generated; ground truth answers are computed algorithmically from the constructed family structures (for ATC) or from the inserted needle content (for information-sparse tasks). For ATC, ground truth is determined by the generation algorithm: for ELDEST_ANCESTOR questions, the answer is name_1; for NTH_ANCESTOR, the answer is name_1; for NTH_DESCENDANT, the answer is name_{n+1}; for RELATIONSHIP_DISTANCE, the answer is total_gen. Approximately 10% of observed errors from the ATC task were manually annotated to identify error types.
rai:dataBiases: The paper explicitly uses synthetic data to mitigate prior-knowledge bias: needles are synthetic, abstract, and fictional statements deliberately designed to avoid overlap with any real-world knowledge or pretraining data, preventing models from relying on memorized knowledge instead of actually processing the input. The paper demonstrates that realistic (Wikipedia-based) benchmarks may already be saturated and mainly reflect memorization rather than genuine reasoning capability, with models achieving very high scores on realistic tasks but experiencing substantial drops (often 50-80%) on synthetic tasks. The ATC uses name randomization to prevent memorization and relationship template variation to create linguistic diversity.
rai:dataCollection: NeedleBench is a synthetic benchmark framework. The dataset is programmatically constructed: needles (key information units) are synthetic, abstract, and fictional statements or relational facts deliberately designed to avoid overlap with real-world knowledge or pretraining data. For information-sparse tasks, haystacks are built using passages from the PaulGrahamEssays dataset (English) and the ChineseDomainModelingEval dataset (Chinese). For the information-dense Ancestral Trace Challenge (ATC), synthetic family relationship datasets are generated algorithmically.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The haystack (filler/background) content for English tasks is sourced from the PaulGrahamEssays dataset (Kamradt, 2023), and for Chinese tasks from the ChineseDomainModelingEval dataset (Wei et al., 2023). The needles (key information) are synthetically generated and do not derive from any real-world source.
rai:dataLimitations: NeedleBench is a synthetic benchmark and may not fully reflect the complexity of real-world tasks. The paper acknowledges this limitation explicitly in the conclusion: "NeedleBench is a synthetic benchmark and may not fully reflect the complexity of real-world tasks." Additionally, the benchmark currently focuses on specific task types (retrieval and ancestral reasoning) and may not cover all aspects of long-context understanding.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Needles are inserted at varying depths within the haystack context. For information-sparse tasks, needles are placed at specific positions (beginning, middle, end, and various depths) within extended texts. For the ATC task, all relationship statements are shuffled to eliminate positional bias. Context lengths are varied across multiple intervals (4k, 8k, 32k, 128k, 200k, 1000k, and beyond). Each configuration is repeated R=10 times to enhance result stability.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Token lengths are measured using the GPT-4 tokenizer. A buffer is subtracted from the target context length when generating each input to mitigate the risk of instruction truncation due to tokenizer discrepancies across different models. For the Multi-Needle Reasoning task, model predictions are post-processed to extract only the content inside \boxed{...}.
rai:dataSocialImpact: NeedleBench provides critical insights and targeted evaluation tools essential for understanding and improving the long-context capabilities of LLMs. By identifying the "under-thinking" phenomenon and other failure modes, it highlights areas where current LLMs fall short in reliably handling information-dense, long-context tasks, which is relevant for real-world applications such as legal document retrieval, academic research, and business intelligence aggregation.
rai:dataUseCases: NeedleBench is intended for evaluating the long-context retrieval and reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs). Specific use cases include: (1) assessing LLM performance on information-sparse retrieval tasks (single and multi-needle retrieval); (2) evaluating multi-step reasoning over long contexts; (3) testing information-dense reasoning via the Ancestral Trace Challenge; (4) benchmarking bilingual (English and Chinese) long-context understanding; (5) identifying failure modes such as "under-thinking" in reasoning models.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 tokenizer (tiktoken, https://github.com/openai/tiktoken) is used to measure token lengths for all tasks. A keyword-aware Exact Match (EM) metric is used for automated evaluation of information-sparse tasks. An exact match metric based on \boxed{} format extraction is used for automated evaluation of the ATC task.
